findings.title: include_website_name missing `?` so website_name leaks for restricted TL0 users
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only checks filter methods that end in `?`, so `include_website_name` is never called and `website_name` is always serialized. The field is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. As a result, the website host and path of a TL0 user is exposed to anonymous viewers, even though `website` itself is hidden from them. The method should be renamed to `include_website_name?` and apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` check (or `website_name` added to `untrusted_attributes`). The TL0 spec's attribute list should also cover `website_name`.

findings.title: Same-level subdomain comparison treats unrelated domains as same site
findings.body: When both hosts have the same number of labels (more than 2), the code compares everything after the first label. For a two-part public suffix this goes wrong: with discourse host `forum.co.uk` and website `evil.co.uk`, both reduce to `co.uk` and are judged to be the same site. The full path of a third-party site is then shown. The logic has no notion of the registrable domain.

findings.title: Hostnames compared case-sensitively
findings.body: URI#host preserves the case of the input, so a website like `http://Example.com/user` will not match a Discourse host of `example.com`. Both hosts should be downcased before comparison.
